subject: EmeraldPath Private: inference throttle observed during peak window
messages:
From: Maya Rao <maya.rao@emeraldpath.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: 17:50-18:30 PST p95 spike + 502s (private cluster)

David —

We hit a severe degradation during tonight's peak (17:50–18:30 PST). Symptoms: p95 token latency rose from ~220ms to ~1.6s, request-level 502s increased (approx 4% of requests at peak), and overall throughput collapsed by ~45%. We pulled a quick trace and attached a log bundle (prod-trace-20260719.zip).

This is our private VPC deployment (cluster: emeraldpath-prod, model pinned: rdx-v2-7b-quant). We saw the runtime still on 1.14.2; our autoscaler did not add capacity despite queueing. We are seeing large KV cache growth (snapshot included) and a backlog in the encoder queue.

Customer impact: chat experiences timeouts and retries; some downstream batch jobs retried and hit downstream rate limits. We need an urgent remediation plan and ETA — our SLA window is impacted. Please advise next steps and whether Redwood can route traffic or apply a temporary fallback.

Thanks,
Maya Rao
Head of Platform Engineering | EmeraldPath Health
ops@emeraldpath.com

Attachments: prod-trace-20260719.zip

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: 17:50-18:30 PST p95 spike + 502s (private cluster)

Folks — looping you in. Maya reported a clear production regression in EmeraldPath's private cluster (details above). Immediate asks:

1) Jonas — can you triage the trace bundle and confirm root cause (KV cache growth vs kernel mis-selection vs scheduling)? If KV cache growth, do we have a quick eviction/hotpatch option?
2) Marissa — can you engage the customer and confirm whether they can accept a short model fallback to rdx-v1-3b as a temporary mitigation (we've used this for other customers to keep latency down while we fix the runtime)? Confirm whether data-flow constraints prevent that.
3) Laura — commercial/exec aware: EmeraldPath flagged SLA impact. If remediation will take >4 hours we should offer credits and an exec update.

Action plan I propose now (please confirm):
- Immediate: Jonas to run a targeted diagnostic (compare runtime kernels, check node ~cpu/gpu utilization, inspect autoscaler decisions).
- Short-term mitigation (30–90m): rotate a fraction of traffic to hosted fallback or to rdx-v1-3b on the private cluster; temporarily lower batch cap to reduce queueing.
- If unsuccessful in 90m: escalate to an exec call and run canary rollback to previous runtime we had for EmeraldPath.

Marissa — please coordinate customer comms, ask for any additional traces, and share the SLA window they care about. Jonas — please attach specific commands/patch you will run. I'll keep EmeraldPath and leadership updated.

-David
David Kim
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 18:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: 17:50-18:30 PST p95 spike + 502s (private cluster)

David / Marissa — quick triage notes after reviewing prod-trace-20260719.zip and the node metrics:

What I see:
- KV cache size on shard-3 grew ~3x compared to baseline; this pushed memory pressure up and caused increased paging between host and GPU memory for that shard.
- Autoscaler observed queue length but did not trigger scale due to a conservative threshold combined with a transient decode-time spike (we have a known edge in 1.14.2 where short bursts don't reach scale threshold).
- Several requests show encoder queue timeouts followed by 502s emitted by the local proxy when backend worker dropped the request.

Immediate remediation I recommend (can be executed now):
1) Trigger a manual scale to add one GPU to emeraldpath-prod (command below).
   - /infra/scale --cluster emeraldpath-prod --add-gpu 1 --reason "emergent throttle"
2) Apply a temporary eviction config for KV cache on shard-3 (evict-old-entries policy TTL 90s) to free GPU memory.
   - echo "evict_policy=ttl:90" > /etc/redwood/kvcache/override.conf && systemctl restart redwood-kvcache
3) Reduce batch cap from 64 -> 24 for model rdx-v2-7b-quant on the cluster to reduce encoder queue latency.
   - redwoodctl set batch-cap --cluster emeraldpath-prod --model rdx-v2-7b-quant --cap 24
4) If the above does not restore p95 within 20m, shift 25% traffic to rdx-v1-3b (lower memory footprint) as a staged fallback.

I attached console screenshots (console-screenshots-emeraldpath.png) with the problematic heap growth and the hot memory map. If Marissa confirms customer consent to fallback, I can run the staged shift.

Estimated time-to-impact after executing steps 1–3: 10–25 minutes (depends on GPU allocation slot in their VPC). If we do step 4, latency should return near baseline for the routed traffic.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: console-screenshots-emeraldpath.png

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@emeraldpath.com>, EmeraldPath Ops <ops@emeraldpath.com>

Subject: EmeraldPath incident: exec update and next steps

Maya — thank you for the quick report and for sharing the traces. I wanted to confirm exec-level awareness and our commitment:

- We have the on-call engineering team working the remediation now (Jonas leading technical actions).
- We will aim to restore baseline latency for the affected traffic within the next 4 hours. If we miss that window, Redwood will provide a credit per our mutual action plan (see attached mutual-action-plan.docx).
- Action owners: Jonas (technical lead), Marissa (customer communications), David (incident lead & exec liaison).

Marissa — please send a one-line status update to EmeraldPath every 30 minutes. Maya — please confirm whether EmeraldPath authorizes the temporary fallback to rdx-v1-3b and the manual scale (Jonas' steps 1–3). If yes, we will proceed immediately.

Laura Bennett
